title: Tensor stability of the derived open test object
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an arbitrary open, with all derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] supplied in a common Hom universe. Let R be derived over restriction followed by Modules.overEquiv U [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], and use the shared derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. For B in D(O_X), assume R.map: Hom(B,E) → Hom(R(B),R(E)) is bijective for every E in D(O_X). Then R.map: Hom(B tensor L,E) → Hom(R(B tensor L),R(E)) is bijective for every L,E in D(O_X).

proof.text: Use the exact extension/restriction adjunction and the extension/restriction isomorphism to obtain a derived adjunction J ⊣ R with invertible unit. Precomposition with the counit J(R(B)) → B identifies via adjunction with R.map on Hom(B,E), up to cancellation by the unit. The hypothesis therefore makes precomposition bijective for all E. Yoneda makes this counit invertible. Exactness and the exterior stalk formula imply that B has zero cohomology stalks outside U.

Represent B by a complex P and L by a K-flat resolution Q. Apply stalk tensor vanishing outside U and identify the derived image of Tot(P tensor Q) with B tensor L, using the K-flat first-variable comparison and symmetry.

For C with zero cohomology stalks outside U, the termwise counit of an arbitrary complex representative is invertible on stalks inside U. Outside U its source stalk complex is zero and its target is acyclic. It is thus a stalkwise quasi-isomorphism, hence a quasi-isomorphism of sheaf complexes, and J(R(C)) → C is invertible in the derived category. Apply this to B tensor L. Naturality of restriction and cancellation by the counit and unit turn the adjunction bijection into exactly R.map on Hom(C,E).

proof_origin.based_on: Second reading: explicit reduction following Stacks 00A7 and 08BT, 06YB and 06YH

theorem derivedOpen_tensorHom_bijective
    (X : Scheme.{uX}) (U : X.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ V : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    (B : schemeDerivedCategory X) :
    let R := ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U) ⋙
      Equivalence.functor
        (C := SheafOfModules.{uX} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
        (D := SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
        (Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory
    (∀ E : schemeDerivedCategory X,
      Function.Bijective (fun f : B ⟶ E ↦ R.map f)) →
    ∀ L E : schemeDerivedCategory X,
      Function.Bijective (fun f : B ⊗ L ⟶ E ↦ R.map f)
